decision_conditions: The proposed development, due to its detailed design, size, siting, would result in a cramped overdevelopment of the site and would be out of character with the area, and being unduly intrusive in the streetscene, would  fail to respect the prevailing pattern of residential development within the surrounding area. In addition the development would provide unsatisfactory and unacceptable living conditions for future occupiers of the new dwellinghouse and would impact on the amenities of the   neighbouring properties and does not assess if the site is considered to be of local ecological value. The development is therefore unacceptable in principle contrary to Policies 13 and 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Supplementary Planning Document 14: "Creating Locally Distinctive Places".

The proposed development by reason of its detailed design and limited plot size would constitute an incongruous and wholly inappropriate form of residential development inconsistent with the prevailing pattern of development within the immediate area. As such the proposed dwelling would be harmful to the character of the site and its wider setting and the streetscene contrary to Policies D1, D3, D4 and D6 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and the advice in Supplementary Planning Document 14 'Creating Locally Distinctive Places'.

The proposed large section of glazing at first floor level of the deveelopment, by reason of its siting in close proximity to the side (western boundary) and its elevated position would result in an increase in overlooking and loss of privacy to the adjoining occupiers at No. 65 Montagu Gardens. The proposal would therefore be contrary to Policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and the provisions of 'The Design of Residential Extensions' Supplementary Planning Document 4.

The proposal is considered to be unacceptable on the grounds of housing quality. More particularly the internal arrangements of the proposed dwelling would provide inadequate provision of natural lighting levels for bedroom 3 on the first floor and inadequate and poor quality external amenity space. The proposal would therefore fail to provide a high standard of living accommodation for the future occupiers of this dwelling contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy 9 of Sutton's Local Plan 2018, and Sutton's Urban Design Guide Supplementary Planning Document (SPD) 14 "Creating Locally Distinctive Places".

In the absence of evidence to indicate otherwise, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed development would conserve or enhance biodiversity within this site. As such, the proposed development is contrary to Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as inserted by Schedule 14 of the Environment Act 2021).
